title: Allow specifying subsecond granularity with tshark -t
description:
Implements suggestion in issue #18714.

Proposed syntax for setting subsecond precission is "tshark -t adoy.3" for
millisecond accuracy in output. Using a dot separator indicates the precission
of what follows the dot in the output.

The following tshark -t combinations are supported:

1. Specifying just the format with e.g. "-t a" and defaulting the precision.
2. Specifying both format and precission, with "-t ad.2" or "-t ad -t .2".
3. Specifying only the precission with "-t .6" and defaulting format.

Using a dot like this avoids introducing a new command line option.

Closes #18714

Other than that grammar issue, I think this looks good and handles Wireshark and Logray as well. Could you also squash the commits when changing that?

Thank you.

I am updating the fix with the following one line changes:

- Add the "be".
- Update commandline.c to also show the new -t format for wireshark/logray -h.
- Update the output in docbook/wsug_src/tshark-h.txt and wireshark-h.txt

However, I realised one thing that bothers me: wireshark and logray default
to whatever setting you have in the gui, and -t updates that as a recent change.
Currently there is no way to say "use auto precision". 

I see a few possibilities for handling that:

1. Ignore this, people can always change back in the gui. This is already somewhat
   the case for the usual -t options, except that with -t, all options are available.

2. Do not update recent settings in WiresharkMainWindow::applyGlobalCommandLineOptions().
   This is different from the usual -t options, but I suspect most people using -t .N
   would do that as a one-off.

3. Introduce "-t .a" (simplest) or "-t .auto" to enforce auto precission. This would
   need something like TS_PREC_NOT_SET as a default that needs handling in other code,
   or TS_PREC_AUTO_REQURESTED that the callers of dissect_opts_handle_opt() must check.

Any thoughts on that before I push?

I think for consistency with the other two timestamp options having it set the recent value and having a command line option makes sense.

From a user perspective I wonder if "." with nothing following is less surprising than ".a"?

Or perhaps a rule of "if precision is not specified, then that means auto precision" (leaving `-t` with no argument as an error still.)

I'm not sure

> `Invalid .N time stamp precision \"%s\"; it must be 0, 1, 2, 3, 6 or 9`

Perhaps either

`Invalid .N time stamp precision \"%s\"; N must be 0, 1, 2, 3, 6 or 9`

or

`Invalid .N time stamp precision \"%s\"; it must be .0, .1, .2, .3, .6 or .9`

Or is it sufficiently obvious that it's referring to the number N in ".N" that this isn't necessary?

The usage help in [ui/commandline c](ui/commandline.c) should be updated similarly to the tshark one. (Maybe eventually the common options should have a common usage help, like the logging options do.)

I went for "." without a number to specify auto precission from trace.
I kind of like the rationale that you care to specify the dot for precission
but don't want a specific number, working as a fallback to the default.

To allow wireshark/logray to detect that no option was requested, I added
TS_PREC_NOT_SET (akin to TS_NOT_SET) and let timestamp_set_precision()
deal with that value. Currently only tshark would call it with TS_PREC_NOT_SET,
but I felt it was better than special casing the value in more places.

The command line help for tshark/wireshark/logray and docs have been updated, too.
You have an extra s in "precision" here.

commits_data.title: Allow specifying subsecond granularity with tshark -t
commits_data.message:
Allow specifying subsecond granularity with tshark -t

Implements suggestion in issue #18714.

Proposed syntax for setting subsecond precision is "tshark -t adoy.3" for
millisecond accuracy in output. Using a dot separator indicates the precision
of what follows the dot in the output.

The following tshark -t combinations are supported:

1. Specifying just the format with e.g. "-t a" and defaulting the precision.
2. Specifying both format and precision, with "-t ad.2" or "-t ad -t .2".
3. Specifying only the precision with "-t .6" and defaulting format.
4. Use "-t a." or even "-t ." to specify auto precision from trace.

The latter use case is particularly useful with wireshark/logray.

Using a dot like this avoids introducing a new command line option.
